learning_objective: 🎯 Time to close up shop! Learn the final accounting steps to sell off all assets, pay off all outside debts, and distribute the remaining cash among the partners.

main_concepts.simple_explanation: Dissolution of Partnership just means the agreement changed (like admission or retirement), but business continues. Dissolution of the FIRM means the business is shutting down completely and forever.
This is a temporary account opened only once in the lifetime of a firm. You transfer all assets here to 'sell' them, and transfer all outside liabilities here to 'pay' them off.

Sometimes you find an old typewriter or an old unpaid bill that isn't on the Balance Sheet. If you sell the unrecorded asset, money comes in (Bank). If you pay the liability, money goes out. Both go through Realisation.
When closing, there are strict legal rules on who gets paid first: 1. Outside debts (bank loans, creditors). 2. Partner's loans. 3. Partner's Capital. Any cash left is shared in the profit ratio.

fun_activity.title: 🏷️ The Garage Sale Liquidation
fun_activity.instructions: Imagine selling your entire bedroom. You list everything (Transfer Assets). You sell your bed for $100 (Realise Asset). You pay back the $20 you owe your sibling (Pay Liability). Whatever cash is left in your hand is exactly how a Realisation account calculates final payout!

exam_tips: 📌 NEVER transfer Cash/Bank balances, General Reserves, or P&L balances to the Realisation Account. They go directly to the Cash A/c or Partners' Capital A/cs.

📌 If a question is silent about the realization value of a Tangible asset, assume it realized its FULL book value. If silent about an Intangible asset (like Goodwill/Patents), assume it realized ZERO.
📌 If a partner takes over an asset, debit their Capital A/c. If a partner agrees to pay a liability, credit their Capital A/c.
quick_recap: ⭐ The Realisation Account is a Nominal Account used to calculate profit or loss on closing the firm.
⭐ Outside creditors are always paid before any partner gets their capital back.
⭐ Dissolution of a firm automatically means the dissolution of the partnership.
